pages.title: Overview
pages.text: Wind power is the easiest AC source to build early on: one $(item)Wind Turbine Controller$() plus one $(item)Wind Turbine Blades$() is all you need. No fuel, no items consumed.$(br2)Its output depends only on the $(l)height of the controller$() and the weather, so build the tower as high as you can.
A wind turbine example: the controller faces the blades.

pages.title: Wind Turbine Blades
pages.text: The blades must be attached to the side of a block (they need a block behind them for support).

pages.title: Wind Turbine Controller
pages.text: The controller checks the block it faces: it must be Wind Turbine Blades, and the blades' facing must match the controller's.$(br2)A controller accepts only one set of blades; extra ones, or blades one block off, generate nothing. Right-click to open the interface and see the current height and output.

pages.title: Output
pages.text: In clear weather: output ≈ controller height ÷ 5 × multiplier (multiplier defaults to 2.0).$(br)$(li)Y = 64: about 25 EP/s$(li)Y = 128: about 51 EP/s$(li)Y = 200: about 80 EP/s$(br2)There is a minimum output even at negative heights (deep sea, caves).$(br2)Rain and thunderstorms change the output noticeably. The EP/s shown in the interface is the live value.

pages.title: Practical Tips
pages.text: $(li)The controller and the blades can be rotated with a Crowbar; no need to break them if they face the wrong way.$(li)Above Y ≥ 200 the blades spin faster, but that is only cosmetic — output still follows the formula.$(li)A wind controller is an AC source: attach it straight to the Tesla Coil's intake face, or feed it into an AC/DC Converter to charge batteries.
